subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw add a core enforced execution-progress contract for artifact-gated status updates, escalation timers, and post-green follow-through, or keep the current run-lifecycle/watchdog improvements as the supported guardrail surface for now?
rationale: Current main now has adjacent liveness and stale-run protections, but the requested artifact/status/post-green policy would add new enforcement semantics, state ownership, and likely configuration/telemetry surface that needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow execution-progress contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design tracker and require an MVP that builds on diagnostic events and SQLite state without ad hoc files.

options.title: Limit to current liveness guardrails
options.body: Treat the merged run-lifecycle stack as the supported protection and split only concrete status-loop bugs with live evidence.

options.title: Defer artifact-gated status enforcement
options.body: Leave the direction open but do not implement until production traces prove thresholds and post-green policy.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow execution-progress contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design tracker and require an MVP that builds on diagnostic events and SQLite state without ad hoc files.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus owns the most recent adjacent run-lifecycle reliability design and implementation stack, so they are the clearest routing candidate for deciding whether this remaining artifact/status policy should be sponsored.
